title: Fear and Loathing in My WebGPU Sandbox.
author: MattMaxBuilds
selftext:
Been working on **OBJEKT 62** on and off for a few months. It’s currently a huge browser sandbox, and I’m building some lore around what you’re doing out there.

The whole project is AI native. I use all sorts of coding agents and models, basically whatever works for the job. Code, assets, music, sound effects, it’s AI all the way down. I’m directing it, putting it together, and playtesting as I go. The fear and loathing is partly the guy stranded on the planet, and partly me developing the thing. We’re both trying to figure out what’s going on here.

You work for a megacorp that doesn’t really care about you. Your ship is wrecked, comms are down, and you’re harvesting resources and finding parts to get off the planet.

You’re a driller, like your father and his father before him. The company appreciates a family tradition.

The planet was also listed as “uninhabited,” which is starting to feel like a paperwork issue.

There’s some **Myst, Rust, and Asimov** in here. Exploring weird places, working to survive, and finding machines still following instructions from people who are long gone. I want figuring out what those instructions actually mean to be part of uncovering what happened.

I’ve also been pushing the scale in the browser. The charted region is **40 km across**, with authored sites and megastructures over a kilometre tall that you can fly out to, land near, and explore inside. A lot of work has gone into the procedural terrain, geometry, and collision to make that fit together.

I’m no mathematician, but apparently the CPU and GPU have slightly different opinions about trigonometry. So I kept those runtime calls out of the shared terrain calculation. They now mostly agree on where the sand is.

If you saw my last couple of posts about [**Kiln**](https://github.com/instruktlabs/kiln), this is one of the games I’m using it in. I’ve been using coding agents with it to build and iterate on assets, then bringing them into the game and playtesting them. Still a lot of hill to climb on polish.

This is footage from the current build, basically a playtest chopped together to a song I made.

Very much alpha. A full run takes hours, and I haven’t thoroughly tested everything end to end yet. Would be cool to get some other devs poking around and giving honest feedback on what works, what breaks, and whether exploring feels worthwhile. Happy to have people help shape the lore too.
